title: laplace.packet-judgement/2
description: Independent review of exact retained packet return and result artifacts, with a real Git target or non-Git source context. Version 1 remains immutable. Accepted requires independent successful observation, no deficiencies and a current COMPLETE builder/result; session provenance never authorizes paths.

schema_version.description: This schema's $id; the version check-return resolves the validating schema by.

packet.description: The label of the packet being judged, verbatim from the plan.

round.description: Which judgement round this is, 1-based; it is part of the verdict file name and of the banked row id.

max_rounds.description: The plan's max_judge_rounds: after this round the orchestrator rules instead of the judge.

accepted.description: The verdict. True is only legal with at least one own_observations entry whose exit_code is 0 and with no deficiencies.

judged.description: Exact worker return and output identity actually reviewed. The Git alternative retains its candidate; artifact review needs no Git checkout.

kind.description: An actual Git candidate plus exact worker return/output pins.

candidate.description: The commit the judge checked out, which must equal the return's source.candidate.

kind.description: Exact artifact target with no invented Git identity.

scripted_check.description: A real command check or receipt-bound declared-owner read. Existing executable command obligations cannot be satisfied by a generic read.

checked.description: The sample the judge actually read or ran, item by item: the plan's judge_sample is a floor on this list's length, not a suggestion.

item.description: The claim or file:line that was checked.

how.description: The command run or the lines read that checked it.

accepted_subsets.description: The parts of the work that stand, each with the finding that establishes it; a rejection is still a record of what was accepted.

id.description: A stable id for this subset, so round two can be read against round one.

status.description: ACCEPTED when the judge's own observation establishes it; CONTESTED when it does not.

finding.description: What the judge observed, with the file:line or command that observed it.

deficiencies.description: What blocks acceptance. Non-empty requires accepted false; each entry says what done looks like, so the continuation has a target instead of a complaint.

id.description: A stable id, carried into the continuation and into round two.

item.description: The file:line, command or claim the deficiency is about.

problem.description: What is wrong, stated as a defect and not as a preference.

evidence.description: The judge's own observation that shows it.

done_looks_like.description: The checkable state that would close this deficiency.

own_observations.description: Commands actually run or successful declared-owner reads performed in the independent review context. Accepted needs a successful independent observation; context alone is not evidence.

path.description: An existing source, output, patch or evidence path whose bytes are retained; absolute or relative to the declared root.

sha256.description: Exact current retained bytes; never an invented hash or a claim that resumed work replays safely.

review_context.description: Independent review context: an actual checkout, or a distinct read-only review session. The consumer verifies ownership/independence; these paths do not grant authority.

kind.description: Review in a separately declared checkout.
Review through existing owners in a distinct session without a whole checkout copy.

session_id.description: Actual consumer-visible independent review session identity.

read_only.description: Reviewed source/results stay unchanged; the judge may write only its declared findings/return.

command.description: The declared exact check command, even when interruption prevented its execution.

exit_code.description: Observed exit status, or null when no exit status was observed. COMPLETE requires PASSED and zero.

output_tail.description: The check's final output, verbatim, enough of it to read the verdict.

state.description: Whether this exact check passed, failed, was interrupted, or was not run.

kind.description: An actually executed or declared command check.
A declared-owner read; no OS command exit is fabricated.

state.description: Observed execution state of the declared read check.

operation.description: The canonical read operation actually invoked, or declared when NOT_RUN.

payload.description: Exact canonical request payload from the existing read receipt.

receipt_id.description: Existing READ receipt ID from the actual worker/reviewer turn, null when no successful read receipt exists.

output_sha256.description: Existing receipt digest of consulted owner result before attaching receipt metadata.

ok.description: Observed read success, null if not run; validated against the actual receipt/context.

output_tail.description: Observed result or exact reason this read check did not run.

command.description: The exact command run by this independent context.

kind.description: A declared-owner read; no OS command exit is fabricated.

operation.description: The canonical read operation actually invoked, or declared when NOT_RUN.

payload.description: Exact canonical request payload from the existing read receipt.

receipt_id.description: Existing READ receipt ID from the actual worker/reviewer turn, null when no successful read receipt exists.

output_sha256.description: Existing receipt digest of consulted owner result before attaching receipt metadata.

ok.description: Successful owner read bound to the independent judge actual turn/session record.

output_tail.description: Observed result or exact reason this read check did not run.
